newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU cuts molasses import tariff.
newsitem.headline: EU cuts molasses import tariff.

text.p: The European Union's sugar management committee has cut the import duty on cane molasses to 0.05 Ecu per 100 kg from 0.06 Ecu, an EU official said on Thursday.
"The tariff was based on a representative price of 8.16 Ecus per 100 kg," the official added.
The import duty on beet molasses remains suspended at zero based on a representative price of 11.20 Ecus per 100 kg.
The official said no additional sugar production levy was expected for the 1996/97 marketing year (July to June) and there could be a cut in the B-quota levy.

"The European Union's sugar management committee's financial review has shown that there is a cumulative financial surplus for last year and dating back to the 1991/92 marketing year which would mean no additional production levy for 1996/97 and a possible cut in the B-quota levy," the official said.
The current production levy is 39.5 percent of the white sugar intervention price.
The committee, which met on Wednewsday, will continue to review the production levy and a final decision will be reached in two weeks time.
"The forecast is provisional and is subject to change. The figures for the last two months of last year (1995/96) are estimates," the official added.
The committee is to continue a review, begun on Wednesday, of quota levels under the GATT agreement on sugar export limits, the official said.
"The review is largely a technical exercise and there is no sign from discussions which began on Wednesday that a cut is needed," the official said.
The discussion, which a Commission official described as "largely a theoretical practice", will continue at the next management committee meeting on Wednesday.
